bib.title: Agentic Information Retrieval
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v4, 23 Feb 2025); the PDF carries an ACM template placeholder, not a venue

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; section 3.1.1-3.1.2 (profile, memory modules) and the life-assistant case study read quickly

question: What changes when the object an IR system retrieves is no longer an item in a fixed corpus but the user's evolving context?
hypothesis: IR should be redefined from acquiring relevant information items to steering the user to a target information state, with an LLM agent as the policy.
contributions: Defines the information state, action, policy, state-transition graph and a verifier-based reward, and states the objective max over pi of E[r(s*, tau)] (Eq. 1)
Shows traditional IR as the special case with state limited to retrieved items and actions limited to filtering a corpus
Maps the agent components (profile, memory, planning, action), single and multi-agent designs and training methods onto IR
Proposes trajectory-level evaluation: utility, efficiency and ethics metrics
Two illustrative case studies (life assistant, business assistant) and open challenges

method.summary: Perspective paper: conceptual formalism and a survey-style mapping, no experiments, no datasets, no results table.

metrics.name: task success rate (TSR)
metrics.definition: similarity of achieved final state s_T to target state s*, binary or partial

metrics.name: run time, token consumption, interaction turns

results.claim: The paper reports no measured result; its claims are definitions and design proposals.
results.quote: in this perspective paper, we introduce the concept of agentic information retrieval

results.claim: Traditional IR is a special case of agentic IR when the information state is confined to the retrieved items shown to the user and the action space to filtering a predefined corpus.
results.quote: agentic IR reduces to traditional IR, making the latter a special case

results.claim: Evaluation should move from list-level (relevance, diversity, fairness) to trajectory-level: a verifier r(s*, tau) compares the target state with the whole trajectory; comparing against one ground-truth trajectory is biased because several trajectories reach the same final state.
The agent's capabilities are bounded by its tools: without a reservation API it can retrieve flight options but cannot book.

limits: Perspective paper: no experiment, benchmark or measured number supports the claims.
The case studies cite commercial products (Apple Intelligence, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Notion AI, IBM watsonx) without evaluating them.
The state-transition graph is defined over the user's state 'in the wild' and is not computable; the verifier is left to rule-based judgment, human annotation or an LLM judge.
Training methods (SFT, preference learning, RFT, reward models) are listed, not compared.

figures.caption: The next paradigm shifts from (a) traditional information retrieval to (b) agentic information retrieval
figures.why: information state transition graph versus corpus lookup
